summary: Little Channel range lights, first exhibited in 1877 at Conway Inlet; the Hardy family kept them until 1947. The surviving rear tower, moved to Freeland, is now a private vacation rental.

light.note: Pole lights set up May 1871 (PEI LHS); station established 1872 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). Range towers first exhibited 20 August 1877 (LighthouseFriends; PEI LHS). Deactivated 1969 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett); PEI LHS says the light was put out in 1968.

range_lights.note: Two range towers. Front: open framework tower 6.1 m (20 ft). Rear: white square wooden tower 9.1 m (30 ft); towers 60.3 m (198 ft) apart.

structures.type: square wooden tower attached to a dwelling
structures.note: Undermined foundation by 1965 (LighthouseFriends). Moved to Freeland (PEI LHS gives 1972; LighthouseFriends gives no date) and now attached to a dwelling roughly 6.4 km from the original site.
No source read says the front range tower survives or when it was removed.

staffing.note: Made unwatched in May 1947 (LighthouseFriends); the Society gives April 1947 for electrification and automation.

access.note: Privately owned; reached by a long private road near Freeland; grounds and tower closed.

visit.note: Best public view is from across the inlet; a distant, partial view is possible from Smith Road (Society).

stay.name: Hardy's Channel Lighthouse Retreat
stay.note: Guests may spend the night in the lighthouse dwelling (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett lists the retreat as owner/site manager).

keepers.name: William Hardy
keepers.note: First keeper per LighthouseFriends, who lists him 1874-1924 as 'William Hardy, Jr.' and says he served roughly fifty years. The 1910 Marine keepers table gives the station as Little Channel and the appointment as 1875; the month is a ditto mark that repeats the row above (May), which the archive.org page image confirms (scan p. 255, printed p. 253), so the story gives the year only. PEI LHS says he began with the 1871 pole lights and continued until 1917.

keepers.name: Ernest A. Hardy
keepers.note: Son of William Hardy. PEI LHS gives 1917 as the start of his keepership. Died May 1946.

keepers.name: Everett L. Hardy
keepers.note: Son of Ernest, appointed after his father's death. The lights were made unwatched in May 1947; he was then paid $15 a year to light and extinguish the range.

corrections.why: The record's agency is the vacation rental that owns the tower; the site is not run by a public agency.

The record lists a second standing 'tower' beside the rear range. The sources describe one surviving tower (the rear), so this entry may duplicate it. No source read describes a surviving front range tower, so the front's status is unknown. An editor should confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: PEI LHS dates the first pole lanterns to May 1871; LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 1872 for the station. The story gives both.

PEI LHS puts the $900 contract to Peter Miller in 1872; LighthouseFriends puts it in 1876, for the two range towers built. The story says the contract went to Miller and gives the LighthouseFriends date for the built range.
PEI LHS quotes a modern article that the light was extinguished in 1968; LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 1969. The story gives 1969 and notes the 1968 date.

The Society's page says the tower was sold and relocated across Conway Narrows to Lighthouse Point, and also that it was moved to Freeland in 1972. LighthouseFriends and Rowlett place it at Freeland. The story gives Freeland and states the Society's Lighthouse Point account.

notes_for_editor: Keepers' dates: the 1910 Marine table prints William Hardy's appointment as 'II 26, 1875' in OCR; the month is probably July (the page image, scan p. 255, printed p. 253, should be checked by an editor before publication). The 1915-16 table repeats a 'July 26, 1875' line beside 'W. Hardy' but the columns are not matched by position, so it is not cited. The end date for William Hardy conflicts: LighthouseFriends 1924, PEI LHS 1917. The first light's date conflicts (1871 PEI LHS vs 1872 LighthouseFriends/Rowlett). The PEI LHS says the rear tower was relocated to 'Lighthouse Point' across Conway Narrows, which conflicts with Freeland, and gives the purchase as 1972; LighthouseFriends and Rowlett describe the Freeland site. Marine reports in the corpus start in 1900, so nothing in the official record covers the 1870s; the 1871-1878 story rests on LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Society, which give the same 1877 date and the same 60.3 m separation. The Wikipedia lead (built 1873; private since 2014) was read only as a lead and is not cited. The corpus Marine reports for FY1917 include a 'moving range lights to new sites' line that lists Little Channel, but the row cannot be matched to the station by position, so it is left out. No newspaper search was run for this station. The Hardy's Channel Lighthouse Retreat is named only as a business, not its owners. Checker pass (2026-10-28): the 1910 keeper row was checked on the archive.org page image (scan p. 255, printed p. 253). The month is a ditto mark, not 'July', so the story gives 1875 only. The story now states the Society's Lighthouse Point account, removes 'the part that survives' (the front range's status is unknown in every source read), and names William Hardy 'Jr.' as LighthouseFriends does.
